answer: At epoch close, each agent's receipt is verified by peers. Receipts include a unique "prism" token, which, if cloned, becomes a "nectar" token with a lower value. A "comet" token, minted for each unique receipt, is used to verify the receipt's authenticity. An attacker cloning 200 receipts would end up with 200 "nectar" tokens, each worth 0.5 of the original "prism" token, resulting in a net loss of 195 tokens.
